still_true: The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy (semaglutide pill) starting doses still cost $149 a month there. The pill's formulation patents keep it brand-only.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands. Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.
No generic tirzepatide exists in the US. Zepbound and Mounjaro are still brand-only, and generic liraglutide remains on the market alongside the new generic semaglutide.
MariTide is still the only monthly incretin on the US market, and no implant has reached patients.
The two EEOC ADA charges over adherence-weighted promotion at a Columbus-corridor logistics firm and a national call-centre operator are still pending without a ruling.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 28.6% ever-used minus 18.4% current gives 10.2% of adults who have used the drugs and are off now. Half of ever-users (14.3 points) have stopped for more than 60 days and restarted. About 11.5 points of those are current users on at least their second course (~62% of current users, up from ~53% because 'skip weeks' and holidays now often run past 60 days), and ~2.8 points cycled and are off again. The remaining ~7.4 points stopped once and never restarted. This is consistent with one-year persistence still near one-third and restart rates at the top of the 36–47% range now that generic semaglutide costs $39–69. Age check: weights 0.20/0.33/0.24/0.23 × 9.5/17.2/26.5/19.5 ≈ 18.4. With ~270M adults that is ~49.7M users. Payer mix: Medicare ~14.0M (28%), the largest single payer. Commercial ~13.0M (26%). Legitimate cash ~12.0M (24%, mostly generic semaglutide at $39–69 plus TrumpRx orals). Medicaid ~6.5M (13%). HRSA free provision ~1.5M (3%). Gray/counterfeit ~2.7M (5.5%, down from 5.2M). Total 49.7M. Public payers combined ~22.0M (44%). Why adoption barely moved when the price collapsed: most of the public expansion is payer substitution, not new users. About 2.4M Medicare beneficiaries switched from brand to generic under old codes, and much of the 3.1M new Medicare obesity-benefit enrolment and most HRSA enrolment came from people who had been paying cash or buying gray-market product. Over the same period, the NAION class warning (Aug 2031), the Novo disclosure scandal and mainstream holiday-taking pulled the 18–49 bands down slightly. The income gap narrowed (top-to-bottom 22 vs 14) because $49 generics, HRSA clinics and 22 Medicaid states displaced the gray market at the bottom. Adult obesity is ~33.6%. Roughly 23% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. They are concentrated in rural non-expansion states and among men 30–49. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s are on a drug, ~2.8% of 12–17s and ~0.3% of 6–11s. Off-label generic semaglutide in under-12s has grown, and Medicaid pays for some of it via EPSDT.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare: the Dec 2031 health package (Medicare Generic Metabolic Access provisions) carves generic incretins (generic semaglutide, generic liraglutide) out of Part D's statutory weight-loss exclusion from Jan 2032 for BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity. Brands still reach Medicare only through the diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes behind prior authorisation. Medicare users ~14.0M: ~5.5M on generic semaglutide (2.4M switchers + 3.1M new-benefit enrollees) at ~$38 net/month = 5.5M × $38 × 12 ≈ $2.5B; ~8.5M on brands (tirzepatide incl. ~2.0M dementia-route, Wegovy pill, retatrutide, MariTide) at ~$240 net = 8.5M × $240 × 12 ≈ $24.5B. Gross Part D incretin spend ≈ $27.0B, down from ~$29.7B in 2030 with 4.1M more users. CBO scored the generic-only benefit at ~$19B over ten years (≈3–5M enrollees × $38 × 12 ≈ $1.4–2.3B a year), against ~$41B for the old brand-inclusive design. Medicaid: the same law sets a 90% federal match for generic incretins, and states covering weight-loss use rose from 9 to 22. ~6.5M users: ~4.5M generic at ~$30 × 12 ≈ $1.6B, ~2.0M brand at ~$245 × 12 ≈ $5.9B, total ≈ $7.5B. HRSA free provision (Mar 2032): ~1.5M uninsured or under-insured adults under 200% FPL get generic semaglutide free at community health centres. 1.5M × ~$30 340B cost × 12 ≈ $540M of a $650M annual appropriation, with the rest for dispensing and labs. Ohio and New Jersey problem-gambling funds pay for ~60,000 of those slots for self-excluded bettors.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $4–30 a month, and Chinese tirzepatide analogues are sold where patents lapsed or were never filed. Several Indian makers are now US ANDA holders, so the US–India price gap has narrowed from ~40× to ~3–5×. Canada's generics run CAD 40–70.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Multiple makers (including an authorised generic from Novo) launched generic semaglutide injection in Dec 2031 under patent settlements. Cash fell to $49 within weeks and to $39–69 by mid-2032 at discount and online pharmacies. Weekly generic pens and vials pulled share back from orals, which fell from ~45% to ~36% of users. Brand prices: TrumpRx oral Wegovy is $149 to start and maintenance fell to $199. Lilly cut Zepbound vials to $249. Retatrutide lists at $1,299 and MariTide at $1,180 (~$299 direct). Wegovy's branded list price of $1,349 is still printed but almost nothing is dispensed at it. Employer coverage recovered from 36% to 40% as generic-first step therapy made coverage cheap. Monitored metabolic tracks now hold ~4.0M people, all inside the ~13.0M commercial users, down from 4.5M as some firms stopped verifying a $40 drug. The gray market shrank to ~2.7M and moved upmarket: counterfeit tirzepatide and retatrutide pens, and 'research' amycretin.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, and generic semaglutide from Dec 2031)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda and generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide). The extension to adults 60+ without CVD received a complete response letter in Jul 2031 pending the confirmatory trial (readout 2033)
alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide/Wegovy pill, approved Jun 2032 on phase 3 data read out Feb 2031; also endorsed in VA/DoD and ASAM guidance, Sep 2031)
gambling disorder: guideline-endorsed, not FDA-labelled (APA conditional recommendation for GLP-1 RAs, Sep 2032, on phase 2 RCTs; a semaglutide phase 3 is enrolling)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: generic semaglutide for AUD by injection, cheaper than the labelled oral
compulsive shopping, screen and sexual compulsion via telehealth and EAPs
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, now mostly on $49 generic semaglutide instead of tirzepatide
low-dose 'steadiness' microdosing, now usually self-titrated from generic vials
generic semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. next_gen_launch = none: no new class reached market. Amycretin had been under review since Oct 2029 and received a complete response letter in Nov 2031. After the Novo NAION disclosure scandal, the FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations had audited Novo's safety submissions, and the letter cited gaps in pooled safety data handling. Resubmission came in Jun 2032, and no decision is expected before 2033. Implant programmes are still phase 1–2. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts read out phase 3 in 2032, and none is filed. The AUD approval is an sNDA for an existing product, filed Apr 2031 and approved after a 14-month review. The compulsion indication is realised through guideline endorsement only. Generic semaglutide came through patent settlements and ANDA approvals (Oct 2031), with launch in Dec 2031. The global incretin market is ~$145B (2031): volumes up, US net prices sharply down on semaglutide. Lilly's tirzepatide and retatrutide carry the brand market.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Restarting after holidays brings GI effects back unless doses are re-titrated, and many self-titrating generic users skip re-titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; the severe gastroparesis caution is retained. Generic labels carry re-titration language after missed doses.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss, and repeated loss-regain cycles may add to it.
Still no causal confirmation for acute pancreatitis, and absolute risk is low. Litigation continues alongside the exocrine claims.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Exocrine-insufficiency filings are consolidating in a new MDL.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years, and ~1.45 in people who have cycled three or more times. Medicare's new generic enrollees are older and less often scanned, so absolute fracture counts are rising in Part D claims.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Jul 2028 class warning is retained. Medicare's generic benefit requires no DXA, and a CMS coverage analysis on DXA for long-term users is open.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A 2031 FDA Sentinel analysis, together with Novo's previously unsubmitted 2026 pooled ophthalmic analysis, puts the HR at ~2.0–2.4. Absolute excess is ~0.5–1 case per 10,000 person-years, highest in people over 60 with diabetes and a crowded optic disc. At ~50M US users that is ~2,500–5,000 excess cases a year, mostly permanent partial vision loss in one eye. Tirzepatide and liraglutide data are thinner but point the same way.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions (Aug 2031) across all GLP-1 RA products, including generics, with a Medication Guide. Baseline eye examination is recommended for anyone with prior NAION or a crowded disc, and patients are told to stop and seek care for sudden vision loss. FMCSA advisory (2032): CDL medical examiners should ask about incretin use.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the flats')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia is ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, and ~10% on retatrutide. The FDA's postmarketing observational study (interim, 2032) reproduces the dose relationship. A 2032 national poll found ~41% of current users had lowered a dose or skipped doses in the past year for mood, pleasure or sex reasons. There are still no randomised data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The oral semaglutide AUD label lists apathy/anhedonia among adverse reactions observed in the AUD trial population. No class labelling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Short holidays (2–6 weeks) produce partial appetite rebound, with modest regain that most users reverse on restart.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. Adherence-conditioned premiums still treat holidays as non-adherence.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency persist in low-intake users, and deficiency rates are higher in HRSA and Medicaid populations with less monitoring.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panels were added to labels for semaglutide-containing products (2031). Uptake in community clinics is incomplete.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Danish and Optum follow-up holds ~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years after year 5 on semaglutide. Early data suggest partial recovery of faecal elastase within 12 months of stopping, and holidays of weeks have no measurable effect. Tirzepatide 5-year exposure now shows a smaller, non-significant excess.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide labels (brand and generic) added EPI to Warnings in 2031, with elastase testing advised for persistent diarrhoea. The class decision is deferred pending tirzepatide data. EMA PRAC recommended semaglutide labelling.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. With generics and public payers, the population expected to take the drug for decades is larger and older. Pediatric bone data from the liraglutide 6–11 postmarketing requirement are due 2033. The interaction of cycling with bone, gallbladder and EPI is unstudied.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric postmarketing requirements continue. CMS and FDA announced a Medicare-claims long-term surveillance cohort tied to the new generic benefit.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Gray-market users fell to ~2.7M as $49 generics undercut Indian vials. Reports now centre on counterfeit tirzepatide and retatrutide pens and 'research' amycretin. Poison-centre calls are down from 2030 but still ~3× 2025, partly from vial dosing errors among self-titrating generic users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The import alert and serialisation remain. FDA guidance on vial dosing devices and labelling for generic semaglutide.

food_and_beverage.state: About 34% of households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~9–10% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~8%. The new decline is in lower-income zip codes, where HRSA and Medicaid users cut value-pack and soda purchases. The premium protein aisle keeps growing in the suburbs. Private-label snack makers report the first sustained volume loss in Southern and Rust Belt markets. Protein ingredient prices eased as pea capacity came online.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~13% from 2025 and beer ~8%. The AUD approval, $49 generics and EAP and Medicaid AUD coverage hit the heaviest-drinking 10% of consumers, who account for over half of volume. State alcohol excise receipts are down mid-single digits. Bar closures have spread from mid-sized Midwestern cities into Appalachian Ohio and West Virginia. Non-alcoholic lines keep growing.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and checks are smaller. Small plates and protein menus are standard. QSR value menus soften in markets where HRSA clinics enrol heavily. Bar-and-grill formats that depended on drink attach rates contract the most.

apparel.state: Plus-size keeps contracting, with Torrid at about half its 2024 store count. Stretch, resale and 'cycle-sizing' subscriptions grow as holidays become routine. Premium structured athletic wear holds at the top.

fitness.state: Strength training and DXA scanning keep growing. Premium clubs still charge $250–400 a month for scan-plus-coaching. Budget chains sell $10 'holiday programmes' to keep weight off between courses. Some community health centres pair the HRSA programme with free group resistance classes, but coverage is patchy.

insurance.state: Employer coverage recovered to 40% on generic-first step therapy, and commercial pharmacy trend slowed to ~+4% in 2032 as semaglutide went generic. Part D premiums rose less than projected because generic substitution offset enrolment growth. Adherence differentials persist and now collide with holiday-taking: wellness vendors added 'clinician-approved holiday' codes that some plans honour and many don't.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue fell by more than half on generics, and the NAION scandal added a DOJ civil investigation and a leadership change. Lilly leads on tirzepatide, retatrutide and dementia, despite the CRL. US generic makers and Indian ANDA holders split the semaglutide market at thin margins. Amgen's MariTide grows inside employer clinics. Sportsbooks report wagering per active account down ~6% year on year in Ohio and New Jersey.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness no longer signals money, because generic semaglutide costs $39–69 a month or nothing at a health centre. What signals money is what surrounds thinness: visible muscle, a recent DXA, good skin, and an eye exam on file. The soft, slightly depleted thin body now reads as generic or public. A regained body reads either as a holiday or as someone who stopped.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle is still the class uniform. In Charlotte and Austin offices people compare lean-mass percentages, and the status move is the managed holiday: two coached weeks off around a wedding or a trip, with protein and lifting to hold the line. On the Columbus logistics corridor, enrollees get a monthly MariTide shot at the plant clinic and look thin without muscle. In Cleveland's east side and the Mississippi Delta, bottom-third women aged 50–64, the regainers of the Bridge-pilot era, are losing weight again on free HRSA semaglutide, and their neighbourhoods are visibly thinner for the first time. Children in commercially insured households remain the medicated pediatric cohort, though Medicaid EPSDT cases are rising.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and protein-forward. 'Skip week' is a social calendar term: people time their holidays for Thanksgiving, weddings and funerals so they can eat with family, and hosts ask who is 'on' when planning menus. The 'Bread Alone' fasting churches claim ~600 congregations and now preach against the free clinics as well as against pharma.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps kept 'lean-mass verified' badges for premium users and added a widely used 'holiday-friendly' tag. Couples schedule holidays around anniversaries and trying to conceive. Monthly MariTide couples can't do that and complain about it.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become something people adjust, not something that just happens to them: dialled down for work, up for holidays. In upper-tier culture, the ability to regulate appetite deliberately is the status marker. In lower-income communities on free generics, appetite is newly quiet, and some read that as relief and others as government sedation. Unmuted and the MAHA wing both say this, from opposite sides.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% of users have clinically meaningful anhedonia (~10% on retatrutide). Around 41% of current users report having adjusted doses or skipped them for mood, pleasure or sex in the past year. 'The flats' is everyday vocabulary.
interior_life.framing: Mostly treated as a side effect that you manage yourself, with dose-downs, skip weeks and summer holidays. The AUD label and the gambling guideline name the drug's effect on reward outright, and that made people ask openly what else it dulls. HR still uses 'steadiness' in competency language, but quietly. Clinicians now ask about pleasure at every refill. Unmuted calls it the free-clinic sedative.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 4.0M workers remain in adherence-verified tracks. Plant-clinic MariTide makes holidays visible to the employer, and verified non-adherence still costs up to 30% in premium differentials under the 2027 guidance. Upper-tier staff take holidays openly and nobody checks. Shift leads at Columbus-corridor warehouses describe holiday weeks as 'loud weeks' and schedule around them. The EEOC charges are still pending.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat' fiction has given way to 'holiday' fiction: novels and streaming series built around the two weeks off. Unmuted 'off nights' have become monthly events in Detroit, Baltimore and Cleveland. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling in Ohio and New Jersey, where state problem-gambling funds pay for semaglutide. Bars near Midwestern plants run 'skip week specials'.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists say holidays have replaced resentment as the main thing couples negotiate. Partners bargain over whose holiday comes when. Libido mismatch is still common, and couples on monthly dosing complain about it most.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Medicare generic benefit passed with bipartisan votes because CBO scored it cheaply. It became a 2032 campaign talking point for both parties in Ohio and Pennsylvania. Ohio's legislature fought over whether sportsbook-tax money should fund a drug that shrinks the betting tax base, and the funding survived narrowly. MAHA legislators cite the Novo scandal against public provision, while Unmuted attacks adherence premiums as penalties on holidays. No new state bans on adherence premiums passed. There is still no turnout evidence for a 'sedated electorate'.

state.regulatory_posture: The FDA is more cautious after the Novo scandal. It issued the NAION class warning, audited Novo's safety submissions, sent a CRL on amycretin, and sent a CRL on the tirzepatide dementia extension pending confirmatory data. It is still fast on generic ANDAs and sNDAs (the AUD approval). Import enforcement is unchanged, and less needed now.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Federal subsidy is now real. The Dec 2031 package added Part D coverage of generic incretins and a 90% Medicaid match, and HRSA's $650M-a-year free provision serves ~1.5M people at community health centres. Ohio and New Jersey problem-gambling funds pay for slots for self-excluded bettors. There is no mandate, and the 2027 30% adherence guidance is unchanged.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: PBM, app and clinic-administration data still flow to wellness vendors. The new channel is Medicare's own long-term surveillance cohort, which makes the federal government both the main payer and the main safety monitor. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress, and holidays longer than 30 days trigger re-authorisation.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE added generic semaglutide to its formulary for existing indications, and its rules are otherwise unchanged. The Army recruit oral pilot continues. FMCSA's 2032 advisory asks CDL examiners to record incretin use and vision symptoms after the NAION warning. DOT still has not ruled on AUD use among drivers, even though AUD is now labelled.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian makers hold several US semaglutide ANDAs, which shifted the India dispute from smuggling to FDA inspections of their plants. Danish politics now centre on Novo's scandal and lost US revenue, not the price gap. China supplies tirzepatide analogues abroad and the counterfeit pen trade into the US.

events.event: Documents unsealed in federal vision-loss litigation show Novo Nordisk's safety unit produced a 2026 pooled trial analysis suggesting roughly doubled NAION risk and recorded it as unconfirmed rather than reporting it to the FDA as a signal. Novo's chief medical officer departs, DOJ opens a civil investigation and Novo shares fall about 20%.

FDA adds a class warning for optic-nerve damage (NAION) to every GLP-1 drug, generics included, recommending baseline eye exams for high-risk patients and immediate stopping for sudden vision loss; Medication Guides are revised

Generic semaglutide injections launch in the US under patent settlements after October ANDA approvals; within six weeks cash prices fall to $49 a month, reaching $39 at some online pharmacies by mid-2032

Congress's year-end health package opens Medicare Part D to generic obesity drugs from January 2032 and sets a 90% federal Medicaid match for them; CBO scores the generic-only design at about $19 billion over ten years, under half the old brand-inclusive estimate

HRSA launches free generic semaglutide at community health centres for adults under 200% of the poverty line with a $650 million annual appropriation; Ohio and New Jersey direct problem-gambling funds to cover self-excluded bettors

FDA approves the Wegovy pill for alcohol use disorder, listing apathy and anhedonia among observed reactions. In September the American Psychiatric Association conditionally endorses GLP-1 drugs for gambling disorder, and clinicians report record requests for dose reductions and 'skip weeks'.

open_tensions: Washington is now the largest payer and the main safety monitor for a drug meant to be taken for decades. It carries two long-horizon warnings (NAION and semaglutide EPI) and a fracture signal concentrated in the older Medicare enrollees it just added, many of whom get no DXA or eye exam.

Drug holidays are now ordinary clinical advice for the flats, yet the 2027 30% adherence-premium guidance and plant-clinic MariTide records still count a holiday as non-adherence. The EEOC charges remain undecided.

States are paying, through problem-gambling funds and Medicaid match, for a drug that shrinks their own sportsbook and alcohol-excise revenue. Ohio's narrow funding vote comes up again in the 2033 budget.

Trust in the label is damaged. Novo faces DOJ and its amycretin resubmission. Lilly's dementia extension waits on a 2033 trial while millions of 50–70-year-olds already take $49 generic semaglutide for dementia prevention off-label.

prose.headline: The $49 Shot: Washington Now Pays for America's Appetite. Americans Take Weeks Off to Feel Things Again.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032, a little more than one American adult in six takes an incretin drug, almost exactly as many as two years ago. The price is what changed. In December 2031 generic semaglutide reached pharmacy shelves under patent settlements, and within weeks the drug that had listed at $1,349 cost $49 for a month of injections. By summer some online pharmacies charged $39. The branded box still prints the old price. Hardly anyone pays it.

The cheap price made a public benefit affordable. In its year-end package Congress opened Medicare to generic obesity drugs and offered states a 90% federal match to cover them in Medicaid. CBO scored the generic-only design at about nineteen billion dollars over a decade, less than half of what had stalled the idea for years. Twenty-two states now cover the drugs. In March, HRSA began handing out generic semaglutide free at community health centres to adults below twice the poverty line. Medicare is now the largest single payer, and public programmes together cover more than four users in ten. Most of these people were already taking the drug. They used to buy it with cash, from Indian vials, or from telegram shops, and now the government pays. The gray market is half its former size and has moved on to counterfeit tirzepatide.

Trust moved the other way. In March 2031, documents unsealed in vision-loss litigation showed that Novo Nordisk's safety staff had pooled their trial data in 2026, seen roughly double the rate of a rare optic-nerve stroke, and recorded it as unconfirmed rather than reporting it as a signal. Executives left, the Justice Department opened an investigation, and in August the FDA put an optic-nerve warning on every drug in the class, generics included. The excess risk is around one case in ten thousand users a year. Across fifty million users that comes to thousands of people a year losing part of the sight in one eye. The agency has since grown more cautious. It sent Novo's next drug back and told Lilly to finish its dementia trial before widening the claim, while millions of people in their fifties and sixties already take $49 generics hoping to protect their memory.

In June the Wegovy pill was approved for alcohol use disorder, and in September psychiatrists endorsed the drug class for gambling. The labels say plainly that the drug dulls reward, and that turned a long-whispered complaint into everyday conversation. People call it the flats. About four in ten users say they have lowered a dose or skipped weeks in the past year to feel more, eat with family or want their partners. 'Skip week' is now a social calendar term. Couples bargain over whose holiday comes when, and people time them for Thanksgiving and funerals. The rules on paper haven't changed: under the 2027 guidance an employer can still charge a worker up to 30% more for missing doses, and at plant clinics where the monthly shot is given, the record shows every gap.

Bodies still sort by income, though thinness no longer separates anyone. In Charlotte and Austin, money shows in the muscle around the thinness, in the scan on file, and in two coached weeks off before a wedding. On Cleveland's east side and in the Delta, women who regained after the old pilot ended are losing weight again on free clinic pens, and their neighbourhoods look thinner for the first time. Ohio pays from its sportsbook tax for gamblers who have self-excluded to take a drug that shrinks the betting tax base, and the legislature kept that funding by a handful of votes. Spirits volumes are down by about an eighth from 2025, and bars are closing in Appalachian Ohio. From the outside the country looks calmer and slightly cheaper to run. The government now pays for a drug meant to be taken for decades, and it is also the one watching for what that does to people.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Teresa Nowak, 59, drives a school bus in Lorain, Ohio, twenty-eight hours a week with no benefits. At 5:40 she sits on the edge of the tub and clicks the pen into her thigh. The pharmacy label says Lorain Family Health Center, quantity 4, patient pays $0.00. Taped to the mirror is a pink Medication Guide page with one paragraph highlighted: sudden loss of vision.

She did her bus medical card in May. The examiner asked whether she was on one of the shots and wrote it down without looking up.

Route 14 is loud, as always. A boy in row six is crying about a lost permission slip. Teresa notices that she doesn't mind it, and then notices herself noticing.

At lunch she eats half a chicken wrap in the cab and texts her sister Dot. *Skipping next week for your sixtieth. Want cake.* Dot replies: *Me too. Mine's the week after, Ray's idea.*

Her husband Ray is 67 and on generic semaglutide through Medicare since January. His copay is $2. Tonight the Browns game is on with the sound low, and he watches with his phone face down on the arm of the recliner. In March he signed the state's self-exclusion form. The betting apps are gone from his phone.

"You want the rest of this?" he asks, holding up a pork chop.

"Next week," she says.

He laughs. It is a real laugh, quieter than the one she married.

At bedtime she writes SKIP on next Tuesday's square on the kitchen calendar, and below it, in smaller letters, *eye dr?*

least_plausible_claims.quote: Over the same period, the NAION class warning (Aug 2031), the Novo disclosure scandal and mainstream holiday-taking pulled the 18–49 bands down slightly.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the candidate asserts that a warning for a risk of about 0.5–1 per 10,000 person-years, plus a corporate scandal, pushed young-adult use down in the same window that cash prices fell about 4x.
